biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin (Hb)
biomarkers.description: Iron-rich protein in red blood cells carrying oxygen from lungs to muscles and tissues.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Tissue hypoxia, fatigue, weakness, cold intolerance, dizziness, microcytic anemia.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Elevated blood viscosity, dehydration, smoking compensation, polycythemia.
foodsToAvoid: Black tea and coffee consumed with iron meals

biomarkers.name: Hematocrit (Hct)
biomarkers.description: Percentage of total blood volume made up of red blood cells.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Reduced oxygen capacity, blood loss, chronic fatigue, nutritional deficiency.

biomarkers.name: Serum Ferritin
biomarkers.description: Intracellular storage protein representing your body's total iron reserves in the liver, spleen, and bone marrow.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Depleted iron reserves, restless legs, hair shedding, brain fog, pre-anemic exhaustion.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Systemic inflammation, hepatic stress, metabolic dysregulation, hemochromatosis.

biomarkers.name: Fasting Blood Glucose
biomarkers.description: Amount of free circulating sugar in your bloodstream after an overnight 8-12 hour fast.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Hypoglycemia, shakiness, autonomic sweating, cognitive impairment, irritability.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Impaired fasting glucose, hepatic insulin resistance, pancreatic stress, pre-diabetes.

biomarkers.name: Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)
biomarkers.description: Percentage of hemoglobin bound to glucose, reflecting your average blood glucose over the past 90-120 days.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Hemolytic anemia, frequent hypoglycemic episodes, shortened red blood cell turnover.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Pre-diabetes (5.7-6.4%), diabetes (>=6.5%), advanced glycation end-products (AGEs), microvascular stress.

biomarkers.name: Total Cholesterol
biomarkers.description: Composite measurement of all sterol lipoproteins (HDL, LDL, VLDL) circulating in your blood.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Impaired steroid hormone synthesis, cellular membrane instability, mood vulnerability.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Excess circulating sterols, potential atherogenic risk depending on particle size and inflammation.

biomarkers.name: LDL Cholesterol
biomarkers.description: Low-density lipoprotein delivering cholesterol from the liver to peripheral tissues; prone to oxidation under inflammatory conditions.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Nutritional malabsorption, severe hyperthyroidism, potential fat-soluble vitamin deficit.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Endothelial plaque accumulation risk, vascular shear stress, oxidized LDL formation.

biomarkers.name: HDL Cholesterol
biomarkers.description: High-density lipoprotein facilitating reverse cholesterol transport from vascular tissue back to the liver for excretion.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Impaired reverse transport, heightened cardiometabolic and atherosclerotic vulnerability.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Usually protective; extreme levels (>100 mg/dL) can sometimes reflect dysfunctional oxidized HDL particles.
foodsToAvoid: Industrial seed oils reheated multiple times

biomarkers.name: Triglycerides
biomarkers.description: Primary storage form of fat in the blood, heavily influenced by recent dietary sugar, alcohol, and carbohydrate consumption.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Malnutrition, extreme hypolipidemia, overactive thyroid function.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Hepatic steatosis (fatty liver risk), metabolic syndrome, pancreatitis risk at severe levels.

biomarkers.name: Vitamin D (25-OH)
biomarkers.description: Secosteroid hormone governing intestinal calcium absorption, immune system regulation, bone mineral density, and gene expression.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Immune vulnerability, seasonal affective slump, bone ache, low mood, muscle weakness.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Hypercalcemia risk, renal calcium deposition (rare unless mega-dosing synthetic supplements).
foodsToAvoid: Excessive processed calcium supplements without K2

biomarkers.name: Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)
biomarkers.description: Crucial coenzyme for red blood cell DNA replication, homocysteine methylation, and myelin nerve sheath preservation.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Peripheral neuropathy, tingling in fingers/toes, megaloblastic anemia, cognitive slowing, elevated homocysteine.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Usually benign (water-soluble); elevated levels can occasionally reflect hepatic release or high supplementation.
foodsToAvoid: Chronic antacid / PPI overuse (impairs intrinsic factor acid)
Excessive alcohol destroying gut mucosal lining

biomarkers.name: Serum Magnesium
biomarkers.description: Intracellular mineral cofactor for over 300 enzymatic processes including ATP energy production, muscle relaxation, and cardiac rhythm.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Muscle spasms, nocturnal leg cramps, sleep disruption, arrhythmia, elevated anxiety.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Depressed deep tendon reflexes, hypotension, renal excretion delay.

biomarkers.name: ALT (SGPT)
biomarkers.description: Hepatic enzyme concentrated in liver hepatocytes; released into bloodstream following liver cellular stress or inflammation.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Generally benign; occasionally associated with vitamin B6 insufficiency or frail muscle mass.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Hepatocellular irritation, non-alcoholic fatty liver (NAFLD), medication stress, alcohol burden.

biomarkers.name: AST (SGOT)
biomarkers.description: Enzyme present in liver tissue, skeletal muscle, and cardiac tissue; indicates cellular repair demand.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Rarely clinically significant; can mirror low B6 or minimal physical demand.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Hepatic or strenuous muscular breakdown, intense eccentric exercise, liver cell stress.
foodsToPrioritize: Brazil nuts (1-2 per day for selenium)

biomarkers.name: Serum Creatinine
biomarkers.description: Natural byproduct of muscular phosphocreatine breakdown, filtered freely by healthy renal glomeruli.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Very low muscle mass, muscular atrophy, severe hepatic dysfunction, inadequate protein intake.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Reduced glomerular filtration rate, acute dehydration, heavy oral creatine supplementation, renal strain.

biomarkers.name: eGFR (Kidney Filtration)
biomarkers.description: Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate calculating how efficiently the kidneys filter waste per minute.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Decreased renal filtration capacity; values below 60 warrant prompt nephrology consultation.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: High hyperfiltration; may occur in early diabetes, severe pregnancy, or high body surface area.

biomarkers.name: Thyroid Stimulating Hormone (TSH)
biomarkers.description: Pituitary hormone instructing the thyroid gland to synthesize thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3).
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Hyperthyroidism, palpitations, heat intolerance, unexplained weight loss, anxiety.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Hypothyroidism (subclinical or clinical), sluggish metabolism, constipation, cold sensitivity, dry skin.
foodsToAvoid: Raw excessive cruciferous veggies (goitrogens - cook them thoroughly)
Soy isolate supplements taken simultaneously with thyroid hormone

biomarkers.name: High-Sensitivity CRP (hs-CRP)
biomarkers.description: Acute-phase hepatic protein that surges in response to systemic vascular inflammation, infection, or tissue injury.
biomarkers.implicationsLow: Excellent low systemic inflammation, favorable vascular baseline.
biomarkers.implicationsHigh: Moderate cardiovascular risk (1.0-3.0 mg/L), high cardiovascular risk or systemic inflammation (>3.0 mg/L).
